question: THE DARK SECTOR'S POWER SPECTRUM: R(k) = 1 (charge, no free streaming; G156/H047) vs lambda_fs = 0.558 Mpc (m = 5.09 keV; G212) -- the two faces, the scale-separation composite P(k) = P_charge + P_dust(smeared), the LSS/CMB/forest/census constraints on the dust fraction, and the k-range that decides

two_faces.charge_face: lambda_fs = 0 EXACT, R(k) = 1 at every k, no cutoff, sub-halo function keeps the CDM power law (H047 N10, G156, G234-a); measured by G215: S_meas = 1.0
two_faces.contrast: 1-R(k): particle face = 0.293 (30) / 0.984 (100) vs charge face = 0.000 at every k: one substance cannot be both; the contradiction is the ontology of the 5.09 keV number (temperature that does not free-stream vs rest mass that does)

composite.model: R_comp(k; f_d) = (1-f_d)*1 + f_d*T^2_WDM(k; m = 5.09) (components add in power; uncorrelated)

des_y3_cmb_k1.reading: blind to f_d: the composite equals R = 1 to 1.7e-4 (0.02% at most, vs ~3% LSS/CMB precision) for ANY dust fraction

budget_pull.source: G234/G115: the free dust is most of the cosmic dark sector (the equilibrium is the few-percent residue)

one_photon_scale_test.definition: the Lyman-alpha flux power at the scale of a single absorption (one photon at one velocity width <-> one comoving scale, k ~ 5-30 h/Mpc)
one_photon_scale_test.reading: 10% flux-power precision at k ~ 30 sees f_d = 0.9 at ~2.6 sigma; the current 95% bound (m > 5.7 keV) is already at this class

deciding_k_range.primary: the sub-halo decade k ~ 100-500 h/Mpc (M ~ 1e5-1e8 Msun, G156's pre-registered dark-halo decade): the faces separate by 40-99% of the dust fraction there; the census (S_meas = 1.0) already leans charge 3.2-4.1 sigma
deciding_k_range.auxiliary: the one-photon-scale forest edge k ~ 10-30 h/Mpc at the cut's visible onset
deciding_k_range.decider: G156's declared rule: differential sub-halo slope <= 0.5 at M_hm in [5e5, 5.8e6] -> RELIC; 1e6-1e7 within [0.5, 1.5] x CDM -> CHARGE

checks.reading: the free-streaming integral is the G093/G115/G212 machinery, digit-faithful

checks.reading: each Ly-alpha line is a one-photon absorption at one physical scale; the flux power at the scale of a single absorption (k ~ 5-30 h/Mpc) coincides with the cut's visible onset -- the test that sees the break BEFORE the census decade does, and its current 95% bound (m > 5.7 keV) is already at this class

checks.reading: not a contradiction-in-principle and not a free lunch: the composite's tension index at budget-required f_d is -3.2 sigma (the pure relic is -3.19), the census leans charge, the forest keeps the particle alive, and G156's declared sub-halo slope measurement is the decider

verdicts.V1: THE TWO-FACE STATEMENT: the dark sector's power spectrum is carried by one number, 5.09 keV, read two ways.  THE CHARGE FACE (G156/H047/G234-a): the sector is the scalar's charge -- lambda_fs = 0 EXACT, R(k) = 1 at EVERY k, no break, the sub-halo mass function keeps its CDM power-law rise (dN/dlnM(1e5)/dN/dlnM(1e7) = 63.1); the census MEASURES it (S_meas = 1.0, N_obs = 19 at the RAR > 1e5 class).  THE PARTICLE FACE (G212/G234-b): the same number is a rest mass -- m = 5.09 +- 0.10 keV, lambda_fs = 0.558 Mpc, k_hm = 57.2 h/Mpc, M_hm = 7.3e+05 Msun, a WARM cut with the sub-halo function inverted below ~1e6 Msun.  THESE CANNOT BOTH BE TRUE OF ONE SUBSTANCE: a 5.09 keV particle suppresses the power by 1-R = 0.29 at k = 30 and 0.98 at k = 100 h/Mpc, while the charge face is R = 1 there to machine precision.  The contradiction is the ontology of the one number: a temperature does not free-stream, a rest mass does.  It is REAL for a single-substance sector and TESTABLE for a two-face one.
verdicts.V2: THE COMPOSITE P(k): the scale-separation hypothesis -- the phantom (equilibrium charge, R = 1) dominating the galaxy/cluster/large scales, the warm dust (lambda_fs = 0.558 Mpc) dominating the sub-halo scales -- is the two-component transfer R_comp(k; f_d) = (1-f_d) + f_d*T^2_WDM(k; m = 5.09): the charge's flat plateau at R = 1 rides under the dust's cut; the break ladder is onset k ~ 1.8 (1/lambda_fs, 1-T^2 = 6.4e-04), 1% at k ~ 6, half-mode at 57 (M_hm = 7.3e+05), saturation 1-f_d above ~300 h/Mpc.  Constraint map: at k <= 1 h/Mpc (DES-Y3/CMB) the composite is CDM to 1.7e-04 for ANY f_d -- the LSS/CMB scales CANNOT see the composition; the forest brackets the dust at the cut's edge (f_d,max(10) = 0.76 under the 5.7 keV record, 0.79 at k = 30); the census binds f_d < 0.28/0.57/0.85 (1/2/3-sigma) at the RAR > 1e5 class; the budget (free dust ~ 98% of the dark sector) pulls the other way: the composite at f_d = 0.98 sits at z = -3.45 vs the census -- the reconciliation is an INDEXED tension, not a free lunch.
verdicts.V3: THE HONEST STATEMENT: the dark sector's power spectrum IS reconcilable as a two-component composite -- the charge face's plateau (R = 1, the equilibrium's: no particle scale) + the warm dust's cut (T^2, lambda_fs = 0.558 Mpc, M_hm = 7.3e+05) -- with the break at k ~ 2-57 h/Mpc separating the charge-dominated large scales from the dust-dominated sub-halo scales.  The reconciliation is NOT free: (1) it requires the dust fraction to be small where the data look: f_d < ~0.76-0.79 across the forest window (the 5.7 keV record rung at 95%), f_d < 0.57 at the sub-halo census (2-sigma, S_meas = 1.0, N_obs = 19) -- while the cosmic budget requires the free dust to be ~98% of the dark sector: the composite's own tension index at the budget fraction is z = -3.45 (vs the pure relic's registered -3.19): the two faces coexist only under a dust fraction the budget and the data pull apart; (2) if 5.09 keV is a temperature (the equilibrium's phase temperature at z*), there is no particle to free-stream at all and the warm-cut language must be withdrawn -- R(k) = 1 stands and the census is right; (3) if 5.09 keV is a rest mass, the cut is real and the census contradicts it at 3.2-4.1 sigma.  THE K-RANGE THAT DECIDES: the sub-halo decade k ~ 100-500 h/Mpc (M ~ 1e5-1e8 Msun -- G156's pre-registered dark-halo decade), where the two faces separate by 40-99% of the dust fraction, with the one-photon-scale test (the single-absorption Lyman-alpha flux power at k ~ 10-30 h/Mpc) as the auxiliary precision test at the cut's visible onset.  G156's rule stands as the decider: measured differential sub-halo slope <= 0.5 at M_hm in [5e5, 5.8e6] -> RELIC (the warm face, the composite with f_d large); 1e6-1e7 within [0.5, 1.5] x CDM -> CHARGE (R(k) = 1, the cut absent, the 5.09 keV read as temperature).  Today's data in the deciding decade lean charge (3.2-4.1 sigma); the forest keeps the particle alive (5.09 inside [3.3, 5.7]).  The two faces are one testable composite, not two truths.

statement: THE DARK SECTOR'S POWER SPECTRUM HAS TWO FACES OF ONE NUMBER.  THE CHARGE FACE (G156/H047): R(k) = 1 at EVERY k, lambda_fs = 0, the census measures no break (S_meas = 1.0, N_obs = 19).  THE PARTICLE FACE (G212): m = 5.09 keV, lambda_fs = 0.558 Mpc, M_hm = 7.3e+05 Msun, a warm cut that alone suppresses the power by 0.29 (30) / 0.98 (100) at k = 30/100 h/Mpc.  One substance cannot be both; the reconciliation is the two-component composite R_comp(k; f_d) = (1-f_d) + f_d*T^2(k; 5.09) -- the charge's plateau at R = 1 with the dust's break at k ~ 2-57 h/Mpc painted on top.  The constraints: DES-Y3/CMB at k ~ 1 is blind (1 - T^2 = 1.7e-4); the forest brackets the dust across its window (f_d,max = 0.76-0.79 under the 5.7 keV record, unbounded at 3.3); the census binds f_d < 0.57 (2-sigma); the budget requires the free dust at ~98% of the dark sector -- the composite at the budget fraction sits at z = -3.45 vs the census (the pure relic is -3.19): an INDEXED tension, not a free lunch and not a contradiction-in-principle.  THE K-RANGE THAT DECIDES is the sub-halo decade k ~ 100-500 h/Mpc (M ~ 1e5-1e8, G156's pre-registration), with the one-photon-scale Lyman-alpha flux power at k ~ 10-30 as the auxiliary test at the cut's visible onset.
